submitter: 283/RFC_032 §10 building thread, Half B (2026-08-24) — the empty-id detector and the render-seam refusal, split out of PLAN_2026-08-24_occurrence_derivation_and_empty_id_detector.md
rationale:
Half B of the ruled RFC_032 §10 build. Half A (deriving the real occurrence from page_components) is NOT in this submission: its only v3_site_actions.go edit sits in a file another session is currently dirty in, and committing it today would mint exactly the same-file passenger that drew the guardian veto on correlation e8c7414c. Half B touches no contested file, so it ships first.

THE DEFECT. A wrong occurrence is only detectable if the detector can see every broken id, and it could not see the worst class at all. reElementID is `\sid="([^"{}]+)"` — the `+` means it cannot match id="" — so an id that rendered LITERALLY EMPTY was invisible to DetectInstanceCollisions and to all three of its callers. Six non-removed page_components rows on six pages across two sites carried one at the time of writing (live DB, 2026-08-24) and every caller read them as clean. Separately, the render seam ALREADY detected the specific cause — component_library.go :1103-1110 tests TemplateNeedsInstanceID and an empty bound token — and only wrote a logger.Error, which this estate has an owner ruling is not escalation (cited at component_library.go:1216).

WHY EMPTY IS ITS OWN CLASS AND NOT A WIDER reElementID. Folding empties into DuplicateElementIDs would fire only at >=2, so a SINGLE empty id — already a defect, since the element is addressable by nothing — would still read clean; it would print an empty string in Summary(); and it would merge two failures with different causes and different remedies. A duplicate id is a wrong OCCURRENCE (bad input to the token rule). An empty id is a failed BINDING, and the corpus proves the two are independent: the live dartsonline pair is category-listing's id="{{.category_slug}}", a CONTENT field, in a template that contains no {{.InstanceID}} at all.

THE AUTHORITY QUESTION, AND WHY THE PLAN'S OWN MEASUREMENT WAS REFUSED. The plan gated arming the refusal on a fleet log census of the Error string, 'expected 0'. That census is a BLIND INSTRUMENT on this cluster and its zero would have been worth nothing: there is no log aggregator in any namespace, spawned job pods carry ttlSecondsAfterFinished=3600, and a sweep of all 181 live and completed pods (176,006 log lines, 2026-08-24) found not one line naming component_library.go — including in the page-rerender pods that had just rendered. A measurement that cannot come out non-zero is not evidence, so it was replaced with three that can, each with a demand control. Those are in grounded_in. On their strength the refusal ships UNCONDITIONAL rather than as an opt-in field: the 2026-08-02 §2 ruling's second arm (measured inert) is satisfied, and a per-caller flag would re-create precisely the per-call-site wiring this seam exists to remove. That trade is named in risks for the seats to take issue with.

plan.summary: Empty element ids become a first-class detector class; the conversion gate hard-errors on them; the render seam REFUSES an {{.InstanceID}} template with no token bound instead of logging; instanceaudit gains the column and a --gate mode that measures the new branch against the live corpus; the offline lint stops probing InstanceID's absence and says so.

edits.rationale: Add the class rather than widen reElementID. One empty id is already a defect, so it must make Clean() false on its own; it has no string to name, so it is counted not listed; and it stays deliberately blind to {{...}} so the existing 'an unrendered template is not evidence' property is preserved (pinned by a control in the test).

The gate's existing id="- check sees only the token-empty shape id="{{.InstanceID}}-suffix". It cannot see id="{{.InstanceID}}" spelled alone — 6 of the 140 active InstanceID templates do exactly that as of 2026-08-24, generic-text-block among them — nor an id whose whole value is another field. HARD error, never the judged pool: the judged pool is for scripts that need rewriting, this is an element nothing can address.

Arm the existing log-only check. The output is structurally wrong for EVERY instance, which is the bugs_open/260 class this seam already enforces — execute or fail, no third state. Deliberately unlike the absent-content report below it, which does not refuse because that content legitimately renders today. Every caller already handles this error channel since 260: rerender carries stored HTML, the editor refuses and leaves the live page, a build fails the step visibly.

REQUIRED BY THE REFUSAL, and found by reading the consumer rather than by a test. InstanceID lives in ContentData, so contextKeys() does not exempt it and the lint's absence probe would remove it and re-render — now an error. The probe-error branch records the field as UNANALYSED, and an unanalysed component's baseline keys count as UNCOVERED, which FAILS the run: arming the seam without this would have pushed all 140 InstanceID templates into that state. Skipped by name and REPORTED on its own line, never silently dropped — the same treatment contextKeys() already gets.

The column is report-only. --gate is the measurement the change owes: it runs the REAL GateConvertedTemplate over every live template that spells the token and reports the outcome classes, breaking the new empty-id branch out from the pre-existing hard errors. It refuses on a zero-considered export for the same reason main already refuses an empty one — a clean report over nothing is not evidence — and exits 3 on any hard error so a CI caller can tell.

The new test asserts CLASS SEPARATION, not just !Clean(), so it cannot pass against the wrong fix (folding empties into DuplicateElementIDs). The existing end-to-end test's mutation control rendered unbound and asserted the output collided; the seam now refuses that render, so the control becomes 'must refuse' AND a second control keeps the collision path exercised on hand-built bytes — otherwise arming the refusal would have quietly retired the only end-to-end duplicate-id test.

Both positive controls are the load-bearing half, per this file's own header. A refusal that also fired on the templates with no {{.InstanceID}} would be a fleet outage rather than a guard, and a gate that refused everything would pass the refusal assertion. All four mechanisms are mutation-proven: reverting the counter, the Clean() term, the gate branch or the return statement each fails a named test, and restoring passes.

grounded_in: STATIC CENSUS, tree-wide, 2026-08-24, with a demand control. Running pattern-check.py's own check_unscoped_component_render over all 972 tracked non-test .go files: 11 files call a RenderTemplate* helper — 6 bind a token (assemble_from_library, component_instance_conversion, rerender_page_sections_action, section_editor_actions, tool_birth_instance_scope, v3_site_actions), 5 are allow-listed in INSTANCE_TOKEN_ALLOWED as once-per-document slots. ZERO unbound. DEMAND CONTROL: substituting the bind call out of each of the 6 flips it to a finding — 6 of 6 'WOULD FIRE' — so the zero could have come out otherwise. (The comment in TemplateNeedsInstanceID still says 'EIGHT non-test files hold FOURTEEN calls', measured 2026-08-16: stale by addition, per CLAUDE.md's dated-count rule.)

ARTEFACT CENSUS, live DB 2026-08-24, with a demand control. Of 2,020 page_components rows, ZERO carry the unbound-token shape id="-…"; 374 carry a bound id="c-…" (the control that proves the query family can find rendered ids at all). 134 of the 140 active InstanceID templates spell id="{{.InstanceID}}-suffix", so that is the shape their unbound render would take.

THE SHARPEST ARM, live DB 2026-08-24. The other 6 templates spell id="{{.InstanceID}}" EXACTLY, so their unbound render is id="" — the only shape where an unbound render is visible as an empty id. generic-text-block is one of them and began spelling it at content_components.updated_at = 2026-08-23 12:32:24+00. In that window 155 of its page_components rows were written: 155 of 155 carry a bound token, 0 empty. Fleet-wide in the same window, 984 rows written, 268 with a bound token, 0 leading-hyphen, 2 empty — and those 2 are the dartsonline pair whose template (category-listing, content_components.updated_at 2026-07-29) is id="{{.category_slug}}" and contains no InstanceID.

THE 6 STORED EMPTY-ID ROWS, re-measured 2026-08-24 (the plan's figure, unchanged): 6 rows / 6 pages / 2 sites, against a denominator of 577 non-removed rows carrying any id attribute. 2 dartsonline (category_slug, above); 4 idea.uk generic-text-block, page_components.updated_at 2026-08-12 17:06–17:11, i.e. ELEVEN DAYS before that template began spelling {{.InstanceID}}. Those 4 carry no c- token, no uuid id and no unrendered braces, so they are not an unbound render of today's template and are owned by the idea_uk_section_data_missing lane.

BLAST RADIUS OF THE REFUSAL, live DB 2026-08-24. Zero chrome templates spell {{.InstanceID}}: header 4, footer 1, site 6, element 1 active rows, all zero. All 140 that do are section (30) or tool (110) level. So the refusal cannot fail a header, footer or <head> render.

BLAST RADIUS OF THE GATE BRANCH, measured with the new tool, 2026-08-24, with a demand control. `instanceaudit templates_active.json --gate` over the 297 active templates ran the REAL gate on the 140 that spell the token: 140 ship as-is, 0 judged-pool, 0 refused by the new empty-id branch, 0 refused by anything else. DEMAND CONTROL: appending one <div id="{{.some_absent_field}}"> to a single row of the same export gives 139 clean / 1 EMPTY-ID and exit 3.

WHY THE PLAN'S LOG CENSUS WAS NOT USED. No log aggregator exists in any of the cluster's 16 namespaces (no loki, fluent, vector, elastic, promtail, otel or datadog pod). Spawned agent jobs carry ttlSecondsAfterFinished=3600. Sweeping all 96 running + 87 completed pods on 2026-08-24 — 176,006 log lines — found 0 occurrences of the target string, and also 0 log lines naming component_library.go at ALL, including in the four agent-page-rerender pods that had just done render work (500 info / 11 warn / 0 error each). The zero measures the instrument, not the fleet.

WHERE THE REFUSAL AND THE WIDENED Clean() ACTUALLY BITE, live config 2026-08-24. enforce_instance_scope appears in exactly 2 active non-snapshot agent_definitions rows: tool-generator and tool-deployer. 3 active agents carry a rerender_page_sections step and NONE is armed, so the rerender sweep's new empty-id term is record-only. The armed path is tool birth (tool_birth_instance_scope.go:49 ScopeToolBirthTemplate), where a refusal is cheap by design — 'the step fails, the work item retries … no live page is waiting on the outcome'.

VERIFIED AT COMMITTED HEAD, not at the working tree. scripts/verify-head-builds.sh --test with only these 7 files overlaid onto HEAD 4358b3f7b: the whole actions package passes. Running the FULL ./... suite twice — pure HEAD, then HEAD+these files — gives an IDENTICAL failure set (differing only in timing digits), so this change adds no failure anywhere in the repo. The 3 TestUpdateWorkItemStatus_* failures visible in the shared working tree are the 345 lane's uncommitted atomic pair (v3_site_actions.go:6212 passing a 7th argument), not this change.
plan.risks:
1. UNCONDITIONAL AUTHORITY ON A SHARED SEAM. The 2026-08-02 §2 ruling prescribes opt-in-with-unsafe-default-OFF for new authority on a shared seam; this ships armed for everyone on the strength of the measured-inert arm instead. The case against a flag: it would put the decision back at each call site, which is the wiring this seam exists to remove, and an unexercised default-OFF switch is a mechanism this estate has been bitten by rotting. The case against arming: my three censuses are all of TODAY's callers and templates, and a caller added tomorrow that renders a section template without binding now FAILS its step rather than shipping a collision. I judge that the better failure, but it is a judgement and it is the seats' to overturn. Note the RFC_022 narrowing does NOT cover this — it exempts opt-in-default-OFF fields with no live consumer, and this is neither.
2. A SECOND DOOR IS LEFT OPEN, deliberately and in writing. RenderTemplateWithMap (rerender_pages_actions.go:818) is an independent render path with no such check and a different template language (bugs_open/260 §13g). Its callers render chrome only and the chrome census is zero, so arming it would guard nothing today — but if a section or tool template ever reaches it, this refusal will not fire. Stated in the code, not just here.
3. I REDUCED WHAT AN AUDIT PROBES. cmd/component-render-check now skips the InstanceID absence probe on ~140 components. It is reported on its own output line and in the JSON (skipped_seam_refusal), never silent, and the alternative was worse — the run would fail on 140 spuriously-uncovered components. But it IS coverage given up, and a seat may reasonably want the probe kept and the lint taught to bind instead.
4. THE DETECTOR IS STILL A REGEX SCAN. reEmptyElementID matches id="" inside a comment or a JS string literal too. It errs toward reporting, like everything else in DetectInstanceCollisions, and the corpus measurement above says it reports nothing today — but a non-empty count remains a reason to look, not proof.
5. WHAT THIS DOES NOT FIX, so no seat has to go looking. The occurrence-0 defect itself (RFC_032 §9c, Half A) is untouched and still live: any per-section render still stamps occurrence 0. The 6 stored empty-id rows are stored BYTES and are not re-rendered by themselves, so nothing here repairs them; they start being RECORDED at their next rerender. Half A follows in a separate submission once v3_site_actions.go is clean enough to edit without a same-file passenger.
